China since the end of the empire: the Republic of China from 1912, and the People's Republic of China, ruled by the Communist Party, from 1949.

Republic (1912 to 1949). The Xinhai Revolution ended the Qing in 1912, and Sun Yat-sen became its first president. Power soon passed to the general Yuan Shikai and then to regional warlords. Students in the May Fourth Movement of 1919 demanded science and democracy. Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists reunited much of the country by 1928, then fought both the Communists and Japan, which took Manchuria in 1931 and invaded in 1937. After Japan's defeat, civil war resumed, and in 1949 the Nationalists retreated to Taiwan, where the Republic of China still exists.

People's Republic (since 1949). Mao Zedong proclaimed the new state on 1 October 1949. Its history falls into two halves:

  • Under Mao: land reform, Soviet-style planning, the Great Leap Forward and the famine it caused, and the Cultural Revolution.
  • After 1978: reform and opening under Deng Xiaoping. Farms went back to families, foreign investment came in through zones like Shenzhen, and growth ran near ten percent a year for three decades. The party crushed the Tiananmen protests in 1989 and kept its monopoly on power.

China joined the World Trade Organization in 2001 and became the world's workshop and its second largest economy. Hundreds of millions left poverty. Under Xi Jinping, since 2012, the party has tightened control at home and grown more assertive abroad. In 2023 India passed it as the most populous country, and its population is now shrinking.
sum: China since the end of the empire: the Republic of China from 1912, and the People's Republic of China, ruled by the Communist Party, from 1949.
